author: Mark Atwood
text:
Workspace-API confidence: ~85% chance the most impactful divergences are caught; ~70% confidence no significant cross-crate divergence is missed.

Highly confident in: capability-surface findings (ops7.5, ops7.6) — file/line verified, behavior obvious. with_tasks_session receiver divergence (ops7.1) — code-grep confirmed. min_date_time type divergence (ops7.9) — file/line verified.

Least confident in:
- ComparatorProperty finding (ops7.15) is a workspace-architectural decision that may already be intentional. The mail-types rustdoc has 25 lines explaining the carve-out; the contacts-types prop::* const module is a deliberate compromise; the absence in filenode/sharing/metadata likely reflects no spec-defined comparator yet. The cross-crate divergence is real, but the right resolution is a workspace decision bead rather than a uniform fix.
- chat-types filter typing (ops7.7) is the right architectural shape per AGENTS.md (silent-drop is a query-correctness bug), but the JMAP Chat draft may not yet specify enough filter clauses to make a typed struct meaningful. The fix shape (empty struct + extras) might be premature optimization until the draft stabilizes.
- README naming inconsistency (ops7.14) is borderline opinion — both names describe the same workspace policy and the metadata-types crate has a genuinely special role.

Uncertainty driven by:
- I surveyed public API surfaces (lib.rs declarations, Cargo.toml, README) but did NOT cross-check trait IMPLs internal to each crate. Cross-crate semantic divergence in default-method behavior (one backend honors a filter field that another silently drops, e.g.) would only show up by reading the MemoryBackend impls. Per AGENTS.md JMAP-ic0j.26 there is a known default-impl-philosophy concern that this review didn't probe.
- I did not run `cargo metadata --format-version 1 | jq '.packages[].dependencies'` to detect transitive version skew across siblings (e.g. divergent serde minor versions).
- I did not check whether all *-server crates' MemoryBackend impls handle the principal_id() seam consistently (AGENTS.md identifies this as a foundation invariant; cross-crate inconsistency here would be a P0).
- I did not survey test-fixture conventions or per-crate AGENTS.md banners for the canonical-template propagation rule.

Recommended follow-up: a future review pass focused on (a) backend default-method behavior parity, (b) transitive dep version skew via cargo metadata, (c) MemoryBackend impl consistency for the principal_id() identity seam.
